versions.agent: Claude Code subagents, same session model in both arms

fixtures: fixtures/13-no-slop: task/ (README spec for the 'Anatomy of Things' explainer-film landing section: hero, 10-language select re-titling 4 film cards from data/films.json with English fallback marked lang=en, m:ss durations, language counts, newsletter form with novalidate + live-region status; synthetic SVG thumbnails), hidden/ (tests.mjs 4 static + 20 browser tests at 390 and 1280, JUDGE.md), reference/ (1.0), grade.mjs (imports the trial-12 harness), KEY.md
design: Arm A = plain subagent builds from the spec; Arm B = same prompt + SKILL.md inline. 3 reps per arm, fresh copies. Score = 0.6 behaviour + 0.2 axe + 0.2 Lighthouse (a11y ≥ 90 and perf ≥ 85). Secondary: slop-marker count and the same blind pairwise judge as trial 12. Pilot (plain agent) scored 0.889, below the ceiling, so no hardening was needed.

candidate_default.config: Arm B with the no-ai-design-slop skill
candidate_default.observed: Every plain run missed the Lighthouse performance bar (83, 74, 82 vs the 85 threshold: fetch-then-inject layout shift and heavier CSS), which costs 0.1 of the score; A-2 also failed one behaviour test. Every skill run passed 24/24 with LH perf 85-86 and 0 slop markers. The skill's review pass (contrast, spacing, 'reserve space for async content') is what pushed CLS and perf over the bar.

candidate_tuned.note: not run; the skill has no knobs

limits: n = 3 per arm; the LH perf margin in arm B is thin (85-86 against an 85 threshold), so part of the 11.5-point gap is a threshold effect on a 0.2-weight component.
Slop markers and the judge are this trial's own secondary metrics; the judge is a model of the same family (blind to arm).
Token counts include each subagent's fixed context; wall time has shared-CPU noise.
verdict: ADOPT for UI-building subagents: +11.5 points (0.885 → 1.000, 3/3 runs at ceiling), 0 slop markers, judge 3:0 for the skill, at +14 % tokens, +40 % tool calls, +48 % time
reason: The only skill trial in this round with a measured primary-score gain: all three skill runs reached 1.0 while all three plain runs lost the Lighthouse component (and one lost a behaviour test). The cost is real (+14 % tokens, about 80 s more per build) but it buys a page that passes the a11y/perf gate first time.
